newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-DORTMUND HIT BY INJURIES TO MOELLER AND KOHLER.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-DORTMUND HIT BY INJURIES TO MOELLER AND KOHLER.

text.p: Borussia Dortmund's preparations for Wednesday's European Cup semifinal with Manchester United were hit by injuries to key German internationals Andy Moeller and Juergen Kohler on Monday.

Kohler, the most experienced defender in the German game, underwent treatment on a badly swollen ankle while midfielder Moeller went to Frankfurt to see a leading physiotherapist because of muscle pains in his legs.

Dortmund already have problems in defence with libero Matthias Sammer suspended for the first-leg tie in Dortmund. Brazilian international defender Julio Cesar also has no chance of making his comeback after a knee injury.
With Sammer out, Moeller is the team's main creative force. It would be a major blow if the midfielder were forced to miss the tie.
Coach Ottmar Hitzfeld said the club's intense campaign in domestic and European football was having an effect on the fitness of players.
"The pressure of matches is taking its toll but we know all about that," Hitzfeld said. "At the moment I can't tell you who is available, never mind give you a line-up."
Hitzfeld's biggest problem is Sammer's replacement. German international wing-back Stefan Reuter and Austrian Wolfgang Feiersinger are the two candidates for the libero position.
But Dortmund know that they will miss Reuter's important attacking influence down the right flank if he is forced to sweep. Feiersinger may be preferred in a defensive role.

The Germans also have injury problems up front. Hitzfeld said he hoped striker Karlheinz Riedle, who has a groin injury, would be fit to return. Swiss forward Stephane Chapuisat also has a back problem but should play.
Moeller said Dortmund had to put the English side under pressure and confuse them if they wanted to win the tie.
"The most important thing is to give the English plenty to do. We have to confront them with situations that they are not used to," the midfielder said.
"We are going to have to put them under so much pressure that they make mistakes. We have to cancel out key players like Ryan Giggs and Eric Cantona."
